**Why sheafifying is what makes an unconditional statement possible.** The
unsheafified functor `picSharp C = T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` is *not*
representable over a general field — it is not even a Zariski sheaf (Kleiman §2
L1292–L1302), and a representable functor is a sheaf for any subcanonical
topology. So an unconditional `RepresentableBy` against `picSharp` would be a
FALSE statement, not merely an unproved one. Against `picEt` it is Kleiman's own
theorem. `PicScheme.picEt_isSheaf_forget` records the sheaf property that makes
the difference, and it is proved rather than assumed.

**Expected to stay open, and that is the honest state rather than a defect.**
Discharging it means formalising the Kleiman §4 existence proof: the Abel-map
slice `Div^d_{C/k} → Pic^d_{C/k}` is a smooth proper equivalence relation whose
quotient is a scheme (`smoothProperQuotient`, itself gated on
`HasSmoothProperQuotient` because Mathlib `v4.31` has no quasi-projectivity
vocabulary), together with `Div` representability (Kleiman §3 Thm `th:repDiv`,
which needs the Quot scheme). Neither input is available; the project reaches
this statement rather than proving it, and it is the single named `sorry` that
the whole Jacobian headline rests on. Do not replace it with a weaker
conditional statement to make a count go down.

This is the **sole** `sorry` of the seam: everything else below — the
representing scheme `PicSchemeEt`, its representability, local finiteness,
separatedness and group-scheme structure, the comparison class
`PicEtComparisonIso` and the conditional `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` — is
derived from it.

**Why the second conjunct is bundled here rather than given its own `sorry`.**
Clause (1) is Kleiman §4; clause (2) is Kleiman §2 Thm 2.5 (`th:comp`): given a
section, the comparison `picSharp C → Pic_{(C/k)ét}` is an isomorphism. Both are
theorems of the same paper and neither is formalised. They are stated as one
named obligation on purpose: the `picSharp`-shaped consumer interface
(`HasPicScheme`, and through it the tangent-space chain and the `k̄` Albanese
witness) needs clause (2) to exist at all, and splitting it out would report the
Jacobian headline as resting on *six* open obligations where the mathematics has
five. The bundling adds no strength — clause (2) is conditional on a section, so
it says nothing about a pointless curve — and it keeps the frontier count honest
in both directions. `scripts/axiom-frontier.lean` measures the result rather
than asserting it. -/

    84	`Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Cartesian/Mon.lean` gives `X ⟶ A` its monoid
    85	structure with `f * h = lift f h ≫ μ[A]` and `1 = toUnit X ≫ η[A]`, but does not
    86	record that *precomposition* respects it. It does, and bundling it as a
    87	`MonoidHom` is what lets `map_prod` move a precomposition through the finite
    88	products below. -/
    89	
    90	/-- **Precomposition with `u : W ⟶ X`, as a monoid homomorphism**
    91	`(X ⟶ A) →* (W ⟶ A)`. Multiplicativity is `comp_lift` (a lift precomposed is the
    92	lift of the precompositions); unitality is uniqueness of the map to the unit
    93	object. -/
    94	noncomputable def preHom {A X W : K} [MonObj A] (u : W ⟶ X) : (X ⟶ A) →* (W ⟶ A) where
    95	  toFun f := u ≫ f
    96	  map_one' := by
    97	    change u ≫ (toUnit X ≫ η[A]) = toUnit W ≫ η[A]
    98	    rw [← Category.assoc]
    99	    congr 1
   100	    exact Subsingleton.elim _ _
   101	  map_mul' f h := by
   102	    change u ≫ (lift f h ≫ μ[A]) = lift (u ≫ f) (u ≫ h) ≫ μ[A]
   103	    rw [← Category.assoc, comp_lift]
   104	
   105	@[simp]
   106	theorem preHom_apply {A X W : K} [MonObj A] (u : W ⟶ X) (f : X ⟶ A) :
   107	    preHom u f = u ≫ f := rfl
   108	
   109	section PermAut
   110	
   111	variable [HasFiniteProducts K]
   112	
   113	/-- **The factor-permuting automorphism of `C^n`.** For `σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)`,
   114	the morphism `C^n ⟶ C^n` whose `i`-th component is the `σ i`-th projection; on
   115	points, `(P₁, …, P_n) ↦ (P_{σ 1}, …, P_{σ n})`. -/
   116	noncomputable def permAut (C : K) {n : ℕ} (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) :
   117	    (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C)) ⟶ (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C)) :=
   118	  Pi.lift (fun i => Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) (σ i))
   119	
   120	omit [CartesianMonoidalCategory K] in
   121	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
   122	theorem permAut_π (C : K) {n : ℕ} (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (i : Fin n) :
   123	    permAut C σ ≫ Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) i = Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) (σ i) := by
   124	  simp only [permAut, Pi.lift_π]
   125	
   126	end PermAut
   127	
   128	section PowSum
   129	
   130	variable [HasFiniteProducts K] [BraidedCategory K]
   131	
   132	/-- **The `n`-fold sum morphism `C^n ⟶ A`.** For `φ : C ⟶ A` into a commutative
   133	group object, the morphism sending `(P₁, …, P_n) ↦ φ(P₁) * ⋯ * φ(P_n)`, formed as
   134	the product in the commutative monoid `(C^n ⟶ A)` of the projections composed
   135	with `φ`.
   136	
   137	In the Albanese application `A` is an abelian variety and the group law is
   138	written additively: this is `(P₁, …, P_g) ↦ φ(P₁) + ⋯ + φ(P_g)`. -/
   139	noncomputable def powSum {C A : K} [MonObj A] [IsCommMonObj A] (n : ℕ) (φ : C ⟶ A) :
   140	    (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C)) ⟶ A :=
   141	  ∏ i, (Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) i ≫ φ)
   142	
   143	/-- **Milne's "clearly this is symmetric".** The `n`-fold sum is invariant under
   144	permuting the factors of `C^n`. The proof is exactly the commutativity of the
   145	group law of `A`: in the *commutative* monoid `(C^n ⟶ A)` a finite product is
   146	invariant under reindexing (`Equiv.prod_comp`).
   147	
   148	This is the hypothesis consumed by the universal property of the symmetric power
   149	`Sym^n C`, which is what licenses the factorisation `C^n ⟶ Sym^n C ⟶ A`. -/
   150	theorem powSum_perm {C A : K} [MonObj A] [IsCommMonObj A] (n : ℕ) (φ : C ⟶ A)

   152	    permAut C σ ≫ powSum n φ = powSum n φ := by
   153	  classical
   154	  calc permAut C σ ≫ powSum n φ
   155	      = ∏ i, (permAut C σ ≫ Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) i ≫ φ) :=
   156	        map_prod (preHom (permAut C σ)) _ Finset.univ
   157	    _ = ∏ i, (Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) (σ i) ≫ φ) :=
   158	        Finset.prod_congr rfl fun i _ => by rw [← Category.assoc, permAut_π]
   159	    _ = ∏ i, (Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) i ≫ φ) :=
   160	        Equiv.prod_comp σ (fun i => Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) i ≫ φ)
   161	
   162	/-- `powSum` is natural in the source: precomposition distributes over the sum. -/
   163	theorem comp_powSum {C A W : K} [MonObj A] [IsCommMonObj A] (n : ℕ) (φ : C ⟶ A)
   164	    (u : W ⟶ (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C))) :
   165	    u ≫ powSum n φ = ∏ i, (u ≫ Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) i ≫ φ) := by
   166	  classical
   167	  exact map_prod (preHom u) _ Finset.univ

     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# Descent of a morphism from a dense open into an abelian variety
    11	
    12	Milne's proof of the Albanese universal property (*Abelian Varieties* III.6
    13	Proposition 6.1) reaches the point "it therefore defines a rational map
    14	`ψ : J ⇢ A`, which (I 3.2) shows to be a regular map". This file supplies that
    15	sentence in the form the Albanese descent actually needs.
    16	
    17	## The statement
    18	
    19	`extend_to_av` (Milne Theorem 3.2, `Albanese/Thm32RationalMapExtension.lean`)
    20	extends a `Scheme.RationalMap` into an abelian variety to a unique morphism.
    21	But a `RationalMap` is a *quotient* of partial maps, so applying it and then
    22	identifying the result requires unfolding that quotient at every call site.
    23	
    24	`exists_unique_hom_restrict_eq_of_dense_open` states the same content in
    25	elementary terms:
    26	
    27	> given a **dense open** `V ⊆ X` and *any* morphism `h : V ⟶ A` into an abelian
    28	> variety which is compatible with the structure maps over `k̄`, there is a
    29	> **unique** morphism `g : X ⟶ A` with `V.ι ≫ g = h`.
    30	
    31	No rational maps appear in the statement. That is the form a descent step wants:
    32	one produces a morphism on the locus where things are defined, and reads back a
    33	morphism on all of `X` together with the equation identifying it there.
    34	
    35	## Why this is the right shape for the Albanese descent
    36	
    37	Milne's `ψ` is built by inverting the birational `f^{(g)} : Sym^g C ⟶ Pic⁰` on
    38	the dense open where it is an isomorphism, and composing with `Sym^g φ`.
    39	Mathlib at this pin has **no** API for inverting a birational morphism (see
    40	`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Birational/{RationalMap,Dominant}.lean`: there is
    41	`IsDominant` machinery but no inverse-on-a-dense-open construction). So the
    42	`Pic⁰ ⇢ A` rational map cannot yet be produced.
    43	
    44	What this file establishes is that *producing it is the only remaining gap*: the
    45	moment one has a dense open `V ⊆ Pic⁰` and a morphism `V ⟶ A` (e.g. a
    46	section of `f^{(g)}` over `V` followed by `Sym^g φ`), the unique global `ψ` and
    47	its defining equation follow with no further geometric input. The extension half
    48	of `descentThroughBirationalSigma` is therefore closed; the birationality half
    49	is what remains.
    50	
    51	## Main results
    52	
    53	* `Scheme.RationalMap.hom_toRationalMap_eq_partialMap_iff` — for a morphism
    54	  `g : X ⟶ A` into an abelian variety and a dense open `V`, the rational-map
    55	  identity `g.toRationalMap = (PartialMap.mk V hV h).toRationalMap` is equivalent
    56	  to the elementary equation `V.ι ≫ g = h`. The bridge that removes the quotient.
    57	* `Scheme.RationalMap.exists_unique_hom_restrict_eq_of_dense_open` — the descent
    58	  statement above.
    59	
    60	## References
    61	
    62	Milne, *Abelian Varieties*, §I.3 Theorem 3.2 and §III.6 Proposition 6.1, p. 104;
    63	blueprint `lem:descent_through_birational_sigma` in
    64	`blueprint/src/chapters/Albanese_AlbaneseUP.tex`.
    65	-/

    72

    74

    76	
    77	variable {kbar : Type u} [Field kbar] [IsAlgClosed kbar]
    78	
    79	/-- **Scheme-level separatedness of an abelian variety.** `A.hom` is separated
    80	(being proper), and `Spec k̄` is affine hence separated over the terminal scheme,
    81	so the composite makes `A.left` separated. Extracted because both results below
    82	need it as an instance. -/
    83	theorem isSeparated_left_of_isProper {k : Type u} [Field k]
    84	    (A : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper A.hom] :
    85	    A.left.IsSeparated := by
    86	  haveI : IsSeparated A.hom := inferInstance
    87	  rw [Scheme.isSeparated_iff]
    88	  have heq : terminal.from A.left = A.hom ≫ terminal.from _ := Subsingleton.elim _ _
    89	  rw [heq]; infer_instance
    90	
    91	/-- **Removing the rational-map quotient.** For a morphism `g : X ⟶ A` into an
    92	abelian variety and a dense open `V ⊆ X` carrying `h : V ⟶ A`, the identity of
    93	rational maps `g.toRationalMap = ⟦(V, h)⟧` is *equivalent* to the elementary
    94	equation `V.ι ≫ g = h`.
    95	
    96	Both directions are the reduced-and-separated agreement principle
    97	(`PartialMap.equiv_iff_of_isSeparated_of_le` with the common dense open `V`):
    98	two partial maps from a reduced scheme to a separated one are equivalent exactly
    99	when their restrictions to a common dense open agree, and here one of them is
   100	already defined on all of `X`. -/
   101	theorem hom_toRationalMap_eq_partialMap_iff {k : Type u} [Field k]
   102	    {X : Over (Spec (.of k))} [IsReduced X.left]
   103	    {A : Over (Spec (.of k))} [IsProper A.hom]
   104	    (V : X.left.Opens) (hV : Dense (V : Set X.left)) (h : (V : Scheme) ⟶ A.left)
   105	    (g : X.left ⟶ A.left) :
   106	    g.toRationalMap = (PartialMap.mk V hV h).toRationalMap ↔ V.ι ≫ g = h := by
   107	  haveI : A.left.IsSeparated := isSeparated_left_of_isProper A
   108	  rw [Scheme.Hom.toRationalMap, PartialMap.toRationalMap_eq_iff,
   109	    PartialMap.equiv_iff_of_isSeparated_of_le (S := ⊤_ Scheme) hV le_top le_rfl]
   110	  simp [Scheme.Hom.toPartialMap, PartialMap.restrict]
   111	
   112	/-- **Descent from a dense open into an abelian variety.**
   113	
   114	Let `X` be a nonsingular variety over an algebraically closed field `k̄`, let `A`
   115	be an abelian variety over `k̄`, let `V ⊆ X` be a **dense open**, and let
   116	`h : V ⟶ A` be *any* morphism whose associated partial map is compatible with the
   117	structure morphisms over `k̄`. Then there is a **unique** morphism `g : X ⟶ A`
   118	restricting to `h` on `V`:
   119	
   120	`∃! g : X ⟶ A, V.ι ≫ g = h`.
   121	
   122	Existence is Milne Theorem 3.2 (`extend_to_av`), whose indeterminacy-locus input
   123	— Milne Lemma 3.3 — is proved in `Albanese/Milne33.lean`, so this is
   124	unconditional. Uniqueness is the agreement principle: two morphisms to a
   125	separated scheme agreeing on a dense open of a reduced scheme are equal.
   126	
   127	This is the extension half of `lem:descent_through_birational_sigma`. Note what
   128	it does *not* require: no birationality, no properness of `V`, and nothing about
   129	where `h` came from. Consequently the remaining gap in the Albanese descent is
   130	purely the construction of the dense open and the morphism on it (i.e. inverting
   131	`f^{(g)}` where it is an isomorphism), not the extension. -/
   132	theorem exists_unique_hom_restrict_eq_of_dense_open
   133	    {X : Over (Spec (.of kbar))}
   134	    [Smooth X.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible X.hom] [IsSeparated X.hom]
   135	    [LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom] [IsIntegral X.left] [IsReduced X.left]
   136	    {A : Over (Spec (.of kbar))}
   137	    [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom] [Smooth A.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom]
   138	    (V : X.left.Opens) (hV : Dense (V : Set X.left)) (h : (V : Scheme) ⟶ A.left)
   139	    (hover : (PartialMap.mk V hV h).toRationalMap.compHom A.hom
   140	      = X.hom.toRationalMap) :
   141	    ∃! g : X.left ⟶ A.left, V.ι ≫ g = h := by
   142	  obtain ⟨g, hg, huniq⟩ := extend_to_av (PartialMap.mk V hV h).toRationalMap hover
   143	  exact ⟨g, (hom_toRationalMap_eq_partialMap_iff V hV h g).mp hg,
   144	    fun g' hg' => huniq g' ((hom_toRationalMap_eq_partialMap_iff V hV h g').mpr hg')⟩
   145	
   146	end Scheme.RationalMap
